title: Why does your phone need airplane mode on a plane?

beats.text: Why does your phone need airplane mode on a plane? Can one phone really crash it?
Movies make it look like your phone can mess with the controls. But no crash has ever been proven to be caused by a phone.
So why the rule? Up here, your phone can't find a signal. So it keeps searching, at full power.
Lower down, at hundreds of miles an hour, it can reach many towers at once. Phone networks were never built for that.
But the real reason is up front. In the cockpit.
Pilots wear headsets. And phone signals can leak in, as a buzzing noise. Like this.
Now imagine 200 phones doing that during landing, when the pilots need to hear every word from the control tower.
So no, your phone won't crash the plane. But it can make the pilots' job harder, at the worst possible moment.
Here's the twist. In Europe, airlines are even allowed to let you use your phone. A tiny mobile mast inside the plane talks to it.
Your phone just whispers to the mast, and everything goes up by satellite.
Bonus: airplane mode also saves your battery, because searching for a signal drains it fast.
So be honest. Do you actually turn it on? Yes or no? Follow Hoot for more.
